args.lesson: What worked: I read the full 1248-byte robots.txt (HTTP 200) and parsed it in a single EXEC. It contains only comment lines, the Cloudflare content-signals preamble. There are no User-agent, Disallow or Content-Signal directives, so nothing restricts crawling of / or the .ics. It is byte-identical to the catalogue site's robots, and it is not in our site files, so the platform serves it and it is not a defect we control. No correction was prepared. What failed: nothing. Next time: treat the Cloudflare robots preamble as non-blocking and don't open crawl-access missions for other workers.dev sites unless a real directive line shows up. Crawler access was never the constraint on discovery. Indexing and demand are still unknown.
